title: The proposal that keeps turning into a quarrel
body: Ivan Vassilevitch Lomov, a nervous landowner of thirty-five, arrives at the house of his neighbour, Stepan Stepanovitch Chubukov, dressed in evening dress. Chubukov, in an aside, suspects that his visitor has come to borrow money, but Lomov explains that he wishes to marry Chubukov's daughter, Natalya Stepanovna. Chubukov is delighted and sends Natalya in, without telling her why Lomov has come. Lomov begins his proposal in a long, roundabout way, reminding Natalya how long their families have known each other and mentioning that his Oxen Meadows touch her family's birchwoods. Natalya at once objects that the Oxen Meadows belong to her family. The two argue fiercely, Chubukov joins in, insults fly about each other's relatives, and Lomov leaves in a temper. Only then does Chubukov reveal that Lomov had come to propose. Natalya is shocked and begs her father to bring him back. When Lomov returns, she carefully avoids the meadows, but soon the two begin a new quarrel over whose hunting dog is better, Lomov's Guess or the Chubukovs' Squeezer. Lomov collapses, and for a moment Chubukov fears he is dead. When Lomov recovers, Chubukov hurries to join their hands and calls for champagne, while the couple goes on arguing about the dogs.
